item.title: TD, BMO named in U.S. debanking investigation report
item.description: A U.S. banking regulator has identified Bank of Montreal and TD Bank, along with seven other lenders, in a report about debanking and limiting access to financial services for certain U.S. customers ...
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: A U.S. banking regulator has identified Bank of Montreal and TD Bank, along with seven other lenders, in a report about debanking and limiting access to financial services for certain U.S. customers due to their political beliefs. The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency released a report based on findings from a supervisory review of debanking activities at nine of the largest banks it oversees, based on 100,000 complaints at OCC-regulated institutions. The OCC says its review was conducted after an executive order by U.S. President Donald Trump, signed in August of last year, stipulating that Americans should not be denied access to financial services due to religious or political beliefs. Jonathan Gould, the comptroller of the currency, says the named banks “denied, debanked and discriminated against customers and lawful businesses.” TD did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while BMO referred The Canadian Press to a statement from the Bank Policy Institute. The institute, a U.S. industry advocacy group, says that it supports fair access to banking services and has been “working to ensure that government regulations and policies enable banks to serve law-abiding customers.” This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 14, 2026. Daniel Johnson, The Canadian Press

item.title: S&P/TSX composite down nearly 400 points, U.S. markets also slide
item.description: Canada’s main stock index was down more than 350 points amid losses in the base metal and technology sectors, while U.S. stock markets also moved lower.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: TORONTO — Canada’s main stock index fell nearly 400 points, weighed down by losses in the basic materials sector, while U.S. markets were also negative. The S&P/TSX composite index was down 399.52 points at 35,584.46. In New York, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 48.62 points at 51,621.48. The S&P 500 index was down 86.51 points at 7,718.94, while the Nasdaq composite was down 511.51 points at 26,692.87. The Canadian dollar traded for 70.11 cents US compared with 70.31 cents US on Tuesday. The November crude oil contract was up 95 cents US at US$95.09 per barrel. The December gold contract was down US$69.40 at US$4,107.90 an ounce. --- This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 14, 2026.

item.title: B.C. home sales fall 9% in September amid interest rate speculation
item.description: Home sales in British Columbia dipped again in September, with the province’s real estate board saying interest rate hike speculation weighed on the market.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: VANCOUVER — Home sales in British Columbia dipped again in September, with the province’s real estate board saying interest rate hike speculation weighed on the market. The British Columbia Real Estate Association says in a release that just over 5, 250 homes were sold last month, down about 9 per cent from the same month in 2025. Home sales were about 26 per cent lower than the 10-year average for B.C. for the month of September. The association says sales volume for residential transactions in B.C. last month was $4.9 billion, down 11 per cent from a year ago, while the average price on the Multiple Listing Service fell 2.4 per cent to just over $924,000. Association chief economist Brendon Ogmundson says in a statement that the declines come after “an encouraging summer” where B.C. showed signs of recovery, but spiking oil prices have prompted speculation on whether the Bank of Canada will raise interest rates. About 51,000 homes have been sold in B.C. so far in 2026, down about 6 per cent from the same period last year, with sales in September falling year-over-year in every region other than South Peace River and the Kootenays. --- This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 14, 2026.

item.title: Statistics Canada reports building permits up $1.1B in August at $13.6B
item.description: Statistics Canada says the total value of building permits issued in Canada in August rose $1.1 billion month-over-month to $13.6 billion, boosted by strength in the residential sector.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: OTTAWA — Statistics Canada says the total value of building permits issued in Canada in August rose $1.1 billion month-over-month to $13.6 billion, boosted by strength in the residential sector. The agency says construction intentions for the homebuilding sector rose $1.1 billion to $8.5 billion in August. The increase came as permits for multi-unit buildings rose to $5.8 billion, while the total value of permits for single-family homes edged down to $2.6 billion. The value of non-residential building permits edged lower by $29.8 million to $5.1 billion in August. The move came as plans for commercial construction fell $380 million to $2.2 billion, offset in part by a $317.3-million gain in the industrial sector which totalled $1.1 billion. The institutional building component rose $32.9 million to $1.8 billion. This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 14, 2026.
